doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Onyx Club with Stuff Smith, sideman work, Billie Holiday at Carnegie Hall
summary: Jimmy Jones joins the trio, they open at the Onyx Club in 1944, then Levy works with Byas, Garner and others and plays Carnegie Hall with Billie Holiday in 1948.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: we got a job to go to 52nd Street and open in the Onyx Club. And in those days they gave you a long term deal, so the deal was for six months. And Jimmy Jones, I’m sort of ahead of myself, because actually Jimmy Jones joined the group — Raymond Walters was the first pianist with us, and he worked with us maybe in Chicago for maybe about two or three months. And then Jimmy Jones and I had been friends, I knew him as a player and I recommended that he come on with us. And that’s how the real Stuff Smith Trio got together. And then we came to New York and opened in the Onyx Club in August of 1944. And then I met Joe Glaser for the first time — this agent and everything. And as I said I developed an excellent relationship with him, and learned a lot about the inside of the business and how it all worked, which helped me later on when I finally went into that end of the business. We worked there at the Onyx Club — I guess we stayed there about a year. And I think I left, I was the first one to leave the trio. I went with Don Byas for a while, and then did a lot of recordings with Ink Spots and you name it, different jazz groups, and then Errol Garner. I made a series of records with Errol, just four sides actually, for Savoy Records with Errol Garner. And from that, one thing to the other until we get to 1948. In 1948 I got a call from Bobby Tucker to join him to work with Billie Holiday. And Billie Holiday had been in Lexington, Kentucky for a rehab for the dope. And she was coming out, and she was going to do a Carnegie Hall concert. And this was 1948. So we got together, and Denzel Best was the drummer. And we rehearsed out in New Jersey at Bobby Tucker’s house, where Billie Holiday was staying. And rehearsed for that. And I can’t remember the exact date in 1948 that we played Carnegie Hall, but we played it. It was my first time in Carnegie Hall. It was the first time that Carnegie Hall had ever had just a trio playing on stage, you know, so I mean the union made a ruling for the future that you’d have to have a minimum number of twelve musicians to play Carnegie Hall.
